name: Tamsulosin Hydrochloride
sections: White crystalline powder (hydrochloride), sparingly soluble in water.
Generic in the USA since 2010; widely used for medical expulsive therapy of distal ureteric stones. First approval/introduction: Japan 1993 (Yamanouchi, now Astellas); US 1997 (Boehringer Ingelheim).

Blocks alpha-1A and alpha-1D receptors in prostatic, bladder-neck and distal ureteric smooth muscle, improving urinary flow in BPH and facilitating passage of distal ureteric stones. Receptor / target profile: Selective antagonist at alpha-1A and alpha-1D receptors in prostate, bladder neck and ureter.
Summary: Modified release; bioavailability ~100% fasting; Tmax 4–5 h (6–7 h fed). ~99% protein bound. Metabolised by CYP3A4 and CYP2D6. Half-life 9–15 h.
Lower urinary tract symptoms due to benign prostatic hyperplasia
Medical expulsive therapy for distal ureteric stones (off-label)
0.4 mg once daily, 30 minutes after the same meal each day
Swallow whole; do not crush or chew
Dose to be individualised by the treating physician according to clinical response and tolerability.
30 minutes after the same meal each day.
Hollingsworth et al., BMJ 2016 – meta-analysis: alpha-blockers improve passage of larger (5–10 mm) distal ureteric stones.
SUSPEND (Pickard et al., Lancet 2015) – no overall benefit for small stones.
First dose at bedtime may reduce dizziness
Store below 30°C in a dry place, protected from light and moisture. Keep out of the reach of children. Do not use after the expiry date.
